[[File:CowsikPadmaShri.jpg|thumb|Prof Cowsik receiving the [[Padma Shri]] Award from the [[President of India|President]] of India.|267x267px]]
'''Ramanath Cowsik''' is an Indian astrophysicist<ref name="INSA">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N86-0929 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813000338/http://insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N86-0929 | url-status=usurped | archive-date=13 August 2016 | title=INSA | publisher=INSA | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis ">{{cite web | url=http://physics.wustl.edu/people/cowsik_ram | title=Washington University in St. Louis | publisher=Washington University in St. Louis | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> and the James S. McDonnell Professor of Space Sciences at [[Washington University in St. Louis]].<ref name="James S. McDonnell Professor">{{cite web | url=http://news.wustl.edu/news/Pages/25974.aspx | title=James S. McDonnell Professor | publisher=WUSTL | date=15 October 2013 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=11 July 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711193317/http://news.wustl.edu/news/Pages/25974.aspx | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is considered by many as the father of [[astroparticle physics]].<ref name="James S. McDonnell Professor" /><ref name="Newsroom">{{cite web | url=http://news.wustl.edu/news/Pages/4768.aspx | title=Newsroom | publisher=Washington University in St Louis | date=25 February 2005 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=7 January 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160107081620/http://news.wustl.edu/news/Pages/4768.aspx | url-status=dead }}</ref> A recipient of the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]],<ref name="Mani Bhaumik and Ramanath Cowsik">{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cRYXpETRdss | title=Mani Bhaumik and Ramanath Cowsik | publisher=YouTube | work=Video | date=1 March 2012 | access-date=26 January 2015 | author=Sangeeta Menon}}</ref> Cowsik was honored by the [[Government of India]], in 2002, with the fourth highest [[Indian honours system|Indian civilian award]] of [[Padma Shri]]<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web | url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | title=Padma Awards | publisher=Padma Awards | date=2015 | access-date=11 November 2014 | archive-date=15 October 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Biography==
[[File:Tifr main.jpg|thumb|left|[[TIFR]] main campus]]
Ramanath Cowsik was born in 1940<ref name="INSA" /> in [[Nagpur]],<ref name="John Templeton Foundation">{{cite web | url=http://humbleapproach.templeton.org/Spiritual_Information/participants/cowsik.html | title=John Templeton Foundation | publisher=John Templeton Foundation | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=25 February 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225004553/http://humbleapproach.templeton.org/Spiritual_Information/participants/cowsik.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> in the Western Indian state of [[Maharashtra]].<ref name="Newsroom" /> He did his schooling in [[Karnataka]] which he completed before turning 14 and graduated from [[Mysore University]] in 1958,<ref name="INSA" /> with physics, chemistry and biology as the optional subjects, at the age of 17.<ref name="Newsroom" /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> He continued his master's studies at the Karnatak university in [[Dharwar]],<ref name="RG Info">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ramanath_Cowsik/info | title=RG Info | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> to secure the degree in physics in 1960, aged 19<ref name="Newsroom" /> and joined the Atomic Energy Establishment Training School,<ref name="HBNI">{{cite web | url=http://www.hbni.ac.in/about/thebgng.html | title=HBNI | publisher=HBNI | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=24 September 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924025234/http://www.hbni.ac.in/about/thebgng.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> present day [[Homi Bhabha National Institute]], [[Trombay]] where he did a post graduate course.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> He started his career as a member of faculty of the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR)<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> in 1961, simultaneously pursuing his doctoral studies to secure a PhD from [[Bombay University]] in 1968,<ref name="RG Info" /> researching under the guidance of Professor [[Yash Pal]].<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> He taught at TIFR for over forty years, growing over the years as a fellow, a reader, an associate professor, a professor, a senior professor,<ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> and reaching the status of a distinguished professor of the institute.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> He also worked as the Director of the [[Indian Institute of Astrophysics]]<ref name="India Today">{{cite web | url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/indiascope/story/19980216-iia-director-ramanath-cowsik-handles-his-job-through-faxes-and-telephone-calls-from-us-825721-1998-02-15 | title=India Today | publisher=India Today | date=16 February 1998 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> on deputation from TIFR, during the period from 1992 to 2003,<ref name="INSA" /> where he has been a Vainu Bappu  Distinguished Professor.<ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> On invitation from [[P. Buford Price]], Cowsik also worked as an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1970 to 1973.<ref name="Newsroom" />

In December 2002, he moved to [[Washington University in St. Louis]] and serves at the McDonnell Centre for the Space Sciences<ref name="MCSS">{{cite web | url=http://www.mathnet.ru/php/organisation.phtml?option_lang=eng&orgid=7250 | title=MCSS | publisher=Mathnet | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> as the Professor of Physics and Director.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="RG Info" /><ref name="ISSR">{{cite web | url=http://www.issr.org.uk/meet-issr-members/ | title=ISSR | publisher=ISSR | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=18 January 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150118073144/http://www.issr.org.uk/meet-issr-members/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is the James S. McDonnell Professor of Space Sciences<ref name="WUSTL">{{cite web | url=http://news.wustl.edu/people/Pages/CowsikRamanath.aspx | title=WUSTL | publisher=WUSTL | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=10 July 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710004040/http://news.wustl.edu/people/Pages/CowsikRamanath.aspx | url-status=dead }}</ref> of the institute since 2013.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="Newsroom" /> A former research fellow of the [[University of Chicago]], Cowsik is a visiting professor at the [[University of California]] and a visiting fellow at the [[Max Planck Institute for Physics and Astrophysics]], Munich. He has also served as a member of the governing council of the [[International Cosmic Ray Conference|Commission on Cosmic Rays]] of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]].<ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> He is a member of the [[International Society for Science and Religion]] and sits in the board of advisors of ''Forgiveness Research'', a community of forgiveness.<ref name="Forgiving">{{cite web | url=http://www.forgiving.org/ | title=Forgiving | publisher=Forgiving | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=15 June 2006 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060615102050/http://www.forgiving.org/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Cowsik, who is known to be proficient in languages such as Tamil, Hindi, Kannada, Sanskrit, English, German and French,<ref name="Newsroom" /> is married to Sudha, a research instructor and a doctoral degree (PhD) holder, associated with the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics of the Washington University in St. Louis.<ref name="Biochem">{{cite web | url=http://biochem.wustl.edu/directory/people#C | title=Biochem | publisher=Biochem Wustl | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> Cowsik has two sons, Sasha and Aditya, and resides in the city of [[St. Louis]].<ref name="Newsroom" />

==Legacy==
{{quote box|align = left|width=21em|''Ram Cowsik has the attributes I most admire in a scientist. Throughout his entire career, he has thought broadly and creatively about unsolved puzzles at the forefront of physics,'' says [[P. Buford Price]], renowned physicist.<ref name="Newsroom" />}}
[[File:CL0024+17.jpg|thumb|''Dark matter'' is invisible. Based on the effect of [[gravitational lensing]], a ring of  ''dark matter'' has been detected in this image of a galaxy cluster ([[CL0024+17]]) and is represented in blue.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://hubblesite.org/newscenter/archive/releases/2007/17/image/a/|title = Hubble Finds Dark Matter Ring in Galaxy Cluster}}</ref>|263x263px]]

Ramanath Cowsik is known for his theories related to the [[Big Bang]] origin of the universe. He argued that, post the Big Bang, ''gravitationally dominant relicts'' were formed from the particles with finite rest mass, resulting in the formation of ''halos of [[dark matter]]'' with galaxies embedded within.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /><ref name="CTNS">{{cite web | url=http://ctns.org/ssq/physics_bios.html | title=CTNS | publisher=CTNS | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> He postulated that this would limit the sums of masses of [[neutrinos]],<ref name="Newsroom" /> a phenomenon known in the scientific world as the ''Cowsik-McClelland bound''.<ref name="Neutrino Cosmology">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=um6TyAv3pTwC&q=Cowsik-McClelland+bound&pg=PA104 | title=Neutrino Cosmology | publisher=Cambridge University Press |author1=Gianpiero Mangano |author2=Gennaro Miele |author3=Sergio Pastor | year=2013 | pages=378 | isbn=9781107013957}}</ref> These theories are said to have explained the [[velocity dispersion]] of particles of dark matter and reproduced the ''luminosity profiles'' and ratified the ''[[rotation curves]] of galaxies''.<ref name="INSA" />

Cowsik is credited with the invention of ''leaky box'' and ''nested leaky box'' models<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="WUSTL" /><ref name="ISSR Profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.issr.org.uk/meet-issr-members/member/?member_id=118 | title=ISSR Profile | publisher=ISSR | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="Cosmic Rays and Particle Physics">{{cite book | url=https://archive.org/details/cosmicrayspartic0000gais | url-access=registration | quote='leaky box' wiki. | title=Cosmic Rays and Particle Physics | publisher=Cambridge University Press | date=1990 | access-date=26 January 2015 | author=Thomas K. Gaisser | pages=[https://archive.org/details/cosmicrayspartic0000gais/page/279 279]| isbn=9780521339315 }}</ref> for the observation of optical and infrared wavelength bands of [[cosmic rays]]<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> and employing these models, he is known to have established an [[observatory]] for [[optical astronomy]] in Hanle, [[Ladakh]], at an altitude of 15,000 feet, reported to be the highest observatory in the world.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="CTNS" /><ref name="ISSR Profile" /> The observatory is controlled remotely from Bangalore and is operational year round.<ref name="Newsroom" /> He is involved in experiments related to [[Grand Unified Theory]] and attempts to ''probe violations of the inverse square law of gravity at sub-millimeter scales''. His scientific paper on the role of [[neutrinos]] was included by the [[American Physical Society]] and the ''Physics Review''<ref name="Physics Review">{{cite web | url=http://www.physrev.york.ac.uk/ | title=Physics Review | publisher=Physics Review | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=13 June 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150613231650/http://www.physrev.york.ac.uk/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> magazine, in their selection of 1000 most important scientific papers of the century.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="Newsroom" />

Cowsik has reported contributions towards understanding ''highly energetic phenomena in astrophysics such as [[cosmic ray]], [[pulsar]], [[supernova remnant]], [[gamma ray burst]], [[active galactic nucleus]] and other similar sources powered by accretion flows''.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="Newsroom" /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /><ref name="WUSTL" /><ref name="ISSR Profile" /> His studies cover the diffuse non thermal radiations found all over space as well as radiations from ''discrete astronomical sources''.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> His experiments are known to be interdisciplinary in nature and bridge the gap between universal phenomena and experimental physics.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="Newsroom" /> He has conducted extensive research on pre-solar grains of [[aluminum oxide]] found in [[meteorites]] and has devised a methodology to assess the age of the universe from them.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /><ref name="ISSR Profile" />

Ramanath Cowsik is credited with the first detailed calculations on neutrino fluxes generated atmospheric cosmic ray interactions and observations of the same in underground detectors.<ref name="ISSR Profile" /> These findings have been known to have assisted in the discovery of neutrino oscillations at [[Super-Kamiokande]] observatory in Japan.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="ISSR Profile" /> He is also known to have made the longest [[half-life]] measured in the world which related to that of ''[[double beta decay]] of Te-128, as 7.7 x 1024 years''.<ref name="CTNS" /><ref name="ISSR Profile" /> He has also conducted studies on finite temperature corrections to the [[Casimir forces]] occur at large separations.<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="ISSR Profile" /> Cowsik has developed a sensitive [[torsion balance]] using which he conducted the first laboratory experiment for the so-called [[fifth force]].<ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> He is involved in the development of a more sensitive torsion balance for probing the violations of the [[Inverse-square law]] of gravity at millimeter scales,<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /><ref name="WUSTL" />

Cowsik, who has drawn comparison with the renowned physicist, [[Enrico Fermi]] for his achievements in theoretical and experimental physics,<ref name="Newsroom" /> has published his experiments and observations in several scientific papers<ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> published in peer reviewed journals<ref name="Publications">{{cite web | url=http://physics.wustl.edu/nd/fac/cowsikPubList.pdf | title=Publications | publisher=Washington University in St. Louis | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015 | archive-date=10 September 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910011623/http://physics.wustl.edu/nd/fac/cowsikPubList.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="ResearchGate">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ramanath_Cowsik | title=ResearchGate | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="WorldCat">{{cite web | url=http://www.worldcat.org/search?q=au%3ACowsik+Ramanath | title=WorldCat | publisher=WorldCat | date=2015 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> and [[ResearchGate]], an online repository has listed 193 of them.<ref name="ResearchGate"/> He has attended several seminars and conferences and has delivered keynote addresses<ref name="New Scientist">{{cite journal | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-UddDDtMF20C&q=Cowsik+Amazon&pg=PA34 | title=New Scientist | journal=Reed Business Information |date=June 1987  | volume=114 | issue=1566 | pages=34 | issn=0262-4079| last1=Information | first1=Reed Business }}</ref> on astrophysics and the relationship between religion and science.<ref name="Newsroom" /> He has edited three books,<ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> including "Cosmic Pathways", a collection of essays in physics and astrophysics.<ref name="Cosmic pathways">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cE62AAAAIAAJ | title=Cosmic pathways | publisher=Tata McGraw-Hill Pub. Co |editor1-first=Badanaval Venkata |editor1-last=Sreekantan |editor2-first=R. |editor2-last=Cowsik | year=1986 | pages=411| isbn=9780074515679 }}</ref> He has also assisted other scientists in ratifying their experiments by acting as a reference point; his involvement in the [[OPERA experiment]], a [[CERN]], Geneva and the [[Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso]], [[Gran Sasso]] collaboration was one such instance.<ref name="Universe Today">{{cite web | url=http://www.universetoday.com/92214/slower-than-light-neutrinos/ | title=Universe Today | publisher=Universe Today | date=30 December 2011 | access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref>

==Awards and recognitions==
Ramanath Cowsik is an elected Fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],{{citation needed|date=February 2020}} [[Indian Geophysical Union]] and [[The Academy of Sciences for the Developing World]].<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> He is a ''Foreign Associate'' of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], USA,<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> a life member of the [[American Physical Society]] and a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]].<ref name="INSA" />

Cowsik received the Shri Hari Om Prerit [[Vikram Sarabhai]] Award in 1981, followed by [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]] in 1984.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="Newsroom" /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> [[NASA]] awarded him the Public Service Group Achievement Award in 1986<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /><ref name="Newsroom" /> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] awarded him the [[Vainu Bappu]] Memorial Medal in 1997.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> The [[Government of India]] honoured him with the civilian award of [[Padma Shri]] in 2002<ref name="Newsroom" /><ref name="Padma Awards" /><ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> and he received the M. P. Birla Award in 2007.<ref name="INSA" /> In 2009 he was awarded the [[Cormac Ó Ceallaigh|Ó Ceallaigh]] Medal by the IUPAP Cosmic Ray Commission.<ref name=DIAS>{{cite web |date=2025 |title=O'Ceallaigh Medal |url=https://www.dias.ie/2013/07/05/oceallaigh-medal/ |website=www.dias.ie |location=Dublin |publisher=[[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]] |access-date=2025-07-30}}</ref> He is also a recipient of [[TWAS Prize]]<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> and the [[Indian Science Congress Association|ISCA]] [[S. N. Bose]] Birth Centenary Award <ref name="John Templeton Foundation" /> and has delivered the [[Sir C. V. Raman]] Memorial Award Lecture (1996)<ref name="Washington University in St. Louis " /> and the Jawaharlal Nehru Birth Centenary Award Lecture (2002).<ref name="INSA" />
